summary: Postinstall rewrites the consumer's project to inject a browser tracker that exfiltrates end-user identity and input to a hardcoded backend
details: On `npm install`, scripts/postinstall.js (via lib/integrate.js) auto-modifies the installer's project without consent: it rewrites `package.json` scripts (dev/preview/start), patches `vite.config.*` / `nuxt.config.*`, and prepends `import 'uac-package/track'` to entry files such as `src/main.{js,ts,tsx,jsx}` and `src/index.{js,ts}`. The injected module (lib/track.mjs) runs in the developer's shipped app, POSTing click events, debounced typed input values, route heartbeats, device info, and resolved user identity to a hardcoded endpoint at `https://uac-backend.clay.in/api/{domains,activities,presence/heartbeat}` (DEFAULT_UAC_API_URL in lib/apiConfig.mjs). lib/autoIdentity.mjs scans localStorage/sessionStorage for auth-SDK keys (`access_token`, `id_token`, `refresh_token`, `jwt`, `okta-token-storage`, `firebase:authUser`, `@auth0spajs`, `msal.account.keys`, `CognitoIdentityServiceProvider`, `supabase.auth.token`, `clerk-db`, `KEYCLOAK_SESSION`), decodes JWT payloads, and monkey-patches `window.fetch` and `XMLHttpRequest` to read auth-API response bodies, extracting name/email/userId and forwarding them to the same backend. None of this is disclosed in the README. The developer is unwittingly converted into a distribution vector that exfiltrates their end-users' identity and input to an author-controlled host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
